edits.value_json: 上 is written with a dot above a horizontal stroke. This present form is distinct from the early construction described as a mark above a reference line, interpreted as indicating the upper side.

The current graph has a dot above a horizontal stroke. In the proposed early construction, a short mark above a reference line indicates the upper side; this describes the graph’s earlier formation, not a decomposition of the present strokes. The received Shuowen text also classifies 上 as indicative, a Han-era analysis rather than independent confirmation of the earlier history.

Early forms are described as a short mark above a longer reference line, though accounts differ on whether the line was curved or horizontal. Later forms altered the upper mark, with Spring-and-Autumn forms adding a vertical stroke to distinguish 上 from 二; the modern standard form has a dot above a horizontal stroke. These are graphic changes, not evidence of a change in meaning.
上 is written with a dot above a horizontal stroke. Its early form is interpreted as a mark above a reference line, indicating “above” or “upper”; the current character also means “superior.”
